title: While loops
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to repeat instructions with a while loop and stop it safely.

sections.title: What is a while loop?
sections.text: A while loop repeats as long as a condition is True. Python checks the condition before every turn, and stops as soon as it is False.

sections.title: Counting with while
sections.text: count = 1, then while count <= 3: print(count) and count = count + 1. The line count = count + 1 changes the variable, so the condition can become False and the loop can end.

sections.title: Infinite loops
sections.text: If nothing inside the loop ever makes the condition False, the loop never stops. This is called an infinite loop. In Build, a program is always stopped after 5 seconds.

sections.title: for or while?
sections.text: Use for when you know how many times to repeat, or which items to go through. Use while when you repeat until something happens.

examples.title: Example 1: A countdown
examples.code:
count = 3
while count > 0:
    print(count)
    count = count - 1
print("Go!")

examples.title: Example 2: Add up 1 to 4
examples.code:
total = 0
n = 1
while n <= 4:
    total = total + n
    n = n + 1
print(total)

check_questions.code:
n = 1
while n < 4:
    print(n)
    n = n + 1
check_questions.explanation: n is 1, 2 and 3 while n < 4. When n becomes 4 the condition is False, so 4 is not printed.

misconception.1: 4 is not less than 4, so the loop stops before printing it.
misconception.2: n starts at 1, so 1 is printed first.
misconception.3: n = 3 still passes n < 4, so 3 is printed too.

check_questions.prompt: Why does this loop never stop?
options: n never changes, so n < 4 is always True
print is not allowed in a while loop
check_questions.explanation: Nothing changes n, so the condition stays True forever. Adding n = n + 1 fixes it.

misconception.1: print works fine inside a while loop.
misconception.2: The number 4 is not the problem.
misconception.3: while loops do not need a for.

check_questions.code:
count = 3
while count > 0:
    count = count - 1
print(count)
check_questions.explanation: The loop runs until count is 0, and then print(count) shows 0.

misconception.1: The loop keeps going until count > 0 is False.
misconception.3: 1 is a value during the loop, not the last value.

try_it.title: Try It Yourself
try_it.instructions: Change the code so it counts down from 5.
try_it.starter:
